question.text: The intrinsic value of an option can:

answer.text: Never be negative (minimum value is zero)
Be negative for put options only
Be negative when volatility is low

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 70 of the source states that only ITM options have intrinsic value, that ATM and OTM options have zero intrinsic value, and that intrinsic value can never be negative — the minimum possible value for both call and put intrinsic value is zero. The Trap: Holders simply will not exercise when doing so would produce a loss, so the floor at zero is mechanical, not optional. Note: Intrinsic value reflects the immediate exercise value; time value sits on top of it until expiry.
